name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Joed according to Nehemiah 11:7. There are no additional notes or distinguishing details recorded about him beyond this familial and tribal association.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution' and is a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 11:7. This meaning is noted but not indicated as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Meshullam was the son of Joed, and it is inferred that Sallu was his father. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance in the biblical narrative is tied primarily to his identification as a Benjamite and a descendant of Joed, situating him within the post-exilic community described in Nehemiah. His mention helps to affirm the genealogical and tribal continuity of God's people during the restoration period. Though not a central figure, his presence contributes to the historical record of faithful families returning to Jerusalem.
